findings.message: Path traversal vulnerability: the check preventing access outside BASE_DIR was removed. path.join does not prevent escaping the base directory if the requested path contains '..' (e.g., '../../etc/passwd').
findings.suggestion: Restore the path traversal check: const resolved = path.resolve(BASE_DIR, requested); if (resolved !== BASE_DIR && !resolved.startsWith(BASE_DIR + path.sep)) { throw new HttpError(403, "path escapes the documents directory"); }

findings.message: The error handler for the '/files' route is registered after the '/files/:name/meta' route. In Express, error-handling middleware must be registered before the routes it is intended to catch errors for. As currently placed, it will not intercept errors thrown by the '/files/:name/meta' handler (or any other routes defined above it), causing those errors to bypass this custom handler and fall through to the default Express error handler.
findings.suggestion: Move the `router.use("/files", ...)` error-handling middleware to the top of the file, before any `router.get` or other route definitions.
